@@ -1252,3 +1252,76 @@ Generierungsbutton als auch die beiden OpenAI-Entwürfe. Nach Auswahl nutzt der
 Entwurf die breite Einzeldarstellung. Die Vollständigkeitsprüfung bleibt eine
 begrenzte, sichtbare Schlüsselwortlogik und kann weitere bislang unbekannte Synonyme
 übersehen; sie trifft keine juristische Bewertung.
+
+# Ausgewählter Tenor ist mobil zu schmal und Diktat wiederholt Sätze nach Pausen
+
+### Symptom
+
+In der Einzeldarstellung blieb der ausgewählte Tenor zu klein zum konzentrierten
+Lesen. Bei 390 × 844 Pixeln war das Textfeld nur 94 Pixel breit. Außerdem hängte die
+Browser-Spracherkennung nach einer Sprechpause den bereits erkannten ersten Satz
+erneut an, bevor sie den nächsten Satz ergänzte.
+
+### Ursache und Diagnose
+
+Die ausgewählte Fassung erbte die für den Zwei-Spalten-Vergleich gedachte kompakte
+Höhe und Innenbreite. Zusätzlich blieb die 248 Pixel breite Desktop-Seitenleiste auch
+unterhalb des `md`-Breakpoints sichtbar. Beim Diktat wurde bei jedem `onresult` die
+gesamte kumulierte `results`-Liste an den jeweils aktuellen Text angehängt. Die Web
+Speech API liefert nach einer Pause frühere Ergebnisse weiterhin in dieser Liste und
+kennzeichnet nur über `resultIndex`, ab welcher Position sich Resultate geändert
+haben.
+
+### Lösung
+
+Die ausgewählte Fassung verwendet nun eine eigene hohe Lese- und Bearbeitungsansicht
+mit größerer Schrift, 32 Pixel Zeilenhöhe und nahezu der gesamten verfügbaren
+Inhaltsbreite. Die Desktop-Seitenleiste wird auf kleinen Viewports ausgeblendet. Das
+Diktat hält den Text vor Beginn der Aufnahme unverändert fest und verwaltet jedes
+Sprachresultat unter seinem Ergebnisindex. Finale und vorläufige Updates ersetzen
+damit das jeweilige Segment; der sichtbare Text wird aus Basis und geordneten
+Segmenten rekonstruiert und nicht mehr kumulativ an sich selbst angehängt. Beginnt der
+Nutzer während eines laufenden Diktats manuell zu schreiben, wird die Aufnahme
+beendet, damit ein spätes Sprachergebnis die Eingabe nicht überschreibt.
+
+### Verifikation und verbleibende Grenze
+
+Der Logiktest simuliert `erster Satz → Finalisierung → Pause → zweiter Satz` und
+bestätigt jeden Satz genau einmal. Ein Browserlauf mit kontrollierter
+SpeechRecognition-Implementierung ergab exakt
+`Der erste Satz. Nach der Pause folgt Satz zwei.` und keine Konsolenfehler. Die
+ausgewählte Textfläche maß bei 1280 × 720 Pixeln 984 × 440 Pixel und bei 390 × 844
+Pixeln 342 × 473 Pixel; der mobile Dokumentkörper hatte keinen horizontalen
+Überlauf. Erkennungsqualität, Zeichensetzung und Mikrofonfreigabe bleiben Funktionen
+der im jeweiligen Browser verfügbaren Web Speech API.
+
+# Vite liefert nach überlappenden HMR-Änderungen einen veralteten Modulstand
+
+### Symptom
+
+Während der laufenden Bearbeitung zeigte die Tenorhilfe nach einem vollständigen
+Reload die Fehlerseite. Die Browserkonsole meldete `needsMoreContext is not defined`,
+obwohl dieser Bezeichner im aktuellen Quelltext bereits nicht mehr vorkam.
+
+### Ursache und Diagnose
+
+Mehrere zeitlich überlappende Änderungen an `MinimalTenorView.tsx` wurden vom lange
+laufenden Vite-Prozess nacheinander per Hot Module Replacement verarbeitet. Der über
+Port 4173 ausgelieferte transformierte Modultext enthielt noch die alte JSX-Referenz,
+aber nicht mehr deren Deklaration. Der aktuelle Quelltext und der frische
+Produktions-Build enthielten diese inkonsistente Kombination nicht.
+
+### Lösung
+
+Der Vite-Entwicklungsprozess wurde vollständig beendet und auf demselben Host und
+Port neu gestartet. Der bestehende ngrok-Tunnel konnte dadurch unverändert auf das
+frisch geladene Frontend weiterleiten.
+
+### Verifikation und verbleibende Grenze
+
+Nach dem Neustart lud `/tenorhilfe` lokal wieder vollständig. Die mobile
+Einzeldarstellung und der Diktat-Pausenlauf liefen anschließend ohne Konsolenfehler.
+HMR ist nur eine Entwicklungsfunktion; bei erneut überlappenden Dateiänderungen muss
+der Dev-Prozess vor einer Demo sauber neu gestartet werden. Ein erfolgreicher
+Produktions-Build allein repariert den Speicherzustand eines bereits laufenden
+Dev-Prozesses nicht.

+
+# Ausgewählter Tenor ist mobil zu schmal und Diktat wiederholt Sätze nach Pausen
+
+### Symptom
+
+In der Einzeldarstellung blieb der ausgewählte Tenor zu klein zum konzentrierten
+Lesen. Bei 390 × 844 Pixeln war das Textfeld nur 94 Pixel breit. Außerdem hängte die
+Browser-Spracherkennung nach einer Sprechpause den bereits erkannten ersten Satz
+erneut an, bevor sie den nächsten Satz ergänzte.
+
+### Ursache und Diagnose
+
+Die ausgewählte Fassung erbte die für den Zwei-Spalten-Vergleich gedachte kompakte
+Höhe und Innenbreite. Zusätzlich blieb die 248 Pixel breite Desktop-Seitenleiste auch
+unterhalb des `md`-Breakpoints sichtbar. Beim Diktat wurde bei jedem `onresult` die
+gesamte kumulierte `results`-Liste an den jeweils aktuellen Text angehängt. Die Web
+Speech API liefert nach einer Pause frühere Ergebnisse weiterhin in dieser Liste und
+kennzeichnet nur über `resultIndex`, ab welcher Position sich Resultate geändert
+haben.
+
+### Lösung
+
+Die ausgewählte Fassung verwendet nun eine eigene hohe Lese- und Bearbeitungsansicht
+mit größerer Schrift, 32 Pixel Zeilenhöhe und nahezu der gesamten verfügbaren
+Inhaltsbreite. Die Desktop-Seitenleiste wird auf kleinen Viewports ausgeblendet. Das
+Diktat hält den Text vor Beginn der Aufnahme unverändert fest und verwaltet jedes
+Sprachresultat unter seinem Ergebnisindex. Finale und vorläufige Updates ersetzen
+damit das jeweilige Segment; der sichtbare Text wird aus Basis und geordneten
+Segmenten rekonstruiert und nicht mehr kumulativ an sich selbst angehängt. Beginnt der
+Nutzer während eines laufenden Diktats manuell zu schreiben, wird die Aufnahme
+beendet, damit ein spätes Sprachergebnis die Eingabe nicht überschreibt.
+
+### Verifikation und verbleibende Grenze
+
+Der Logiktest simuliert `erster Satz → Finalisierung → Pause → zweiter Satz` und
+bestätigt jeden Satz genau einmal. Ein Browserlauf mit kontrollierter
+SpeechRecognition-Implementierung ergab exakt
+`Der erste Satz. Nach der Pause folgt Satz zwei.` und keine Konsolenfehler. Die
+ausgewählte Textfläche maß bei 1280 × 720 Pixeln 984 × 440 Pixel und bei 390 × 844
+Pixeln 342 × 473 Pixel; der mobile Dokumentkörper hatte keinen horizontalen
+Überlauf. Erkennungsqualität, Zeichensetzung und Mikrofonfreigabe bleiben Funktionen
+der im jeweiligen Browser verfügbaren Web Speech API.
+
+# Vite liefert nach überlappenden HMR-Änderungen einen veralteten Modulstand
+
+### Symptom
+
+Während der laufenden Bearbeitung zeigte die Tenorhilfe nach einem vollständigen
+Reload die Fehlerseite. Die Browserkonsole meldete `needsMoreContext is not defined`,
+obwohl dieser Bezeichner im aktuellen Quelltext bereits nicht mehr vorkam.
+
+### Ursache und Diagnose
+
+Mehrere zeitlich überlappende Änderungen an `MinimalTenorView.tsx` wurden vom lange
+laufenden Vite-Prozess nacheinander per Hot Module Replacement verarbeitet. Der über
+Port 4173 ausgelieferte transformierte Modultext enthielt noch die alte JSX-Referenz,
+aber nicht mehr deren Deklaration. Der aktuelle Quelltext und der frische
+Produktions-Build enthielten diese inkonsistente Kombination nicht.
+
+### Lösung
+
+Der Vite-Entwicklungsprozess wurde vollständig beendet und auf demselben Host und
+Port neu gestartet. Der bestehende ngrok-Tunnel konnte dadurch unverändert auf das
+frisch geladene Frontend weiterleiten.
+
+### Verifikation und verbleibende Grenze
+
+Nach dem Neustart lud `/tenorhilfe` lokal wieder vollständig. Die mobile
+Einzeldarstellung und der Diktat-Pausenlauf liefen anschließend ohne Konsolenfehler.
+HMR ist nur eine Entwicklungsfunktion; bei erneut überlappenden Dateiänderungen muss
+der Dev-Prozess vor einer Demo sauber neu gestartet werden. Ein erfolgreicher
+Produktions-Build allein repariert den Speicherzustand eines bereits laufenden
+Dev-Prozesses nicht.

--- name: minimal-writing-product-design description: Design or implement document-first web products that use a blank writing canvas, content-based follow-up questions, slash modes, keyboard-driven search, inline autocomplete, and a focused two-proposal decision. Use when a user wants the interaction logic of a minimalist AI writing workspace rather than a form, dashboard, wizard, or chat interface. --- # Minimal Writing Product Design Build the product around one continuous act of writing. Controls should appear only when the user's current state makes them useful. Preserve the user's domain, terminology, existing stack, and requested capabilities; reuse this interaction model without copying legal content or assuming a particular business process. ## Establish the product contract Before editing code, derive these domain-specific values from the request and repository: - the object the user is writing or describing; - the minimum semantic facts required before generation is useful; - the modes that materially change how the input is interpreted; - the records, templates, or prior work a search mode should expose; - the two meaningfully different proposal strategies; - which completions may be generated freely and which must come from a trusted library; - what must remain editable and what always requires human confirmation. Do not ask about choices that can be inferred safely. Ask only when one of these values would materially alter the product. ## Preserve the core interaction model 1. Start as an almost empty white page with one instructional placeholder inside the writing surface. 2. Let the same surface accept a new description, an existing draft, pasted text, dictation, or an uploaded source when the product supports them. 3. Replace length thresholds with a transparent semantic completeness check. Ask one specific question for the first important missing fact, directly below the user's text. 4. Reveal the primary action only when the input is semantically sufficient or the current mode supports acting on partial text. 5. Open mode selection when the user types `/`. Make it compact, inline, filterable, and fully keyboard operable. 6. Render the chosen mode as bold inline text immediately before the input. It may be separate state internally, but Backspace at the start of the text must remove it as though it were adjacent text. 7. In search or record-selection modes, filter while the user types. Arrow keys move a visibly selected row; Enter adopts that row. 8. Offer inline autocomplete only when it has a safe next unit to suggest. Tab accepts; ordinary typing never gets intercepted. 9. After generation, present two clearly distinct, editable proposals with a binary choice. Do not create a gallery of near-duplicates. 10. Keep upload, dictation, and the contextual primary action in a restrained bottom bar so the page remains visually open. If the requested product does not need one of these capabilities, omit it rather than adding a decorative or inert control. ## Work in the existing codebase - Inspect the current framework, routing, design tokens, reusable components, and state conventions before implementing. - Preserve the existing architecture and package manager unless the user explicitly requests a replacement. - Separate domain rules from visual components. Completeness, mode interpretation, proposal composition, and trusted autocomplete should be testable without rendering the page. - Use one primary route and one coherent state model. Do not turn the experience into a dashboard or multi-step wizard unless the domain requires it. - Use trusted source IDs, provenance, or human-approval flags wherever the new domain requires traceability. Do not fabricate them to make a demo look complete. - Keep partial functionality honest. An upload control that does not extract content must say so; an unverified proposal must look unverified. ## Route to detailed guidance - Read [references/visual-language.md](references/visual-language.md) before creating or substantially restyling the page. - Read [references/interaction-contract.md](references/interaction-contract.md) when implementing modes, completeness questions, keyboard behavior, search, autocomplete, or proposal selection. - Read [references/implementation-and-acceptance.md](references/implementation-and-acceptance.md) when writing code, defining state, or validating the finished interaction. ## Completion standard The result should feel like writing on a clean sheet, not filling a form. A new user should be able to begin by typing without first understanding the product. Every revealed element must answer the current state: what can I type, what is missing, what can I choose, or what happens next. Validate compilation and relevant tests. For interaction changes, verify the keyboard-only path from empty page through mode selection, optional record selection, generation, proposal choice, editing, and reset. Report any capability that remains simulated or incomplete. --- name: minimal-writing-product-design description: Design or implement document-first web products that use a blank writing canvas, content-based follow-up questions, slash modes, keyboard-driven search, inline autocomplete, and a focused two-proposal decision. Use when a user wants the interaction logic of a minimalist AI writing workspace rather than a form, dashboard, wizard, or chat interface. --- # Minimal Writing Product Design Build the product around one continuous act of writing. Controls should appear only when the user's current state makes them useful. Preserve the user's domain, terminology, existing stack, and requested capabilities; reuse this interaction model without copying legal content or assuming a particular business process. ## Establish the product contract Before editing code, derive these domain-specific values from the request and repository: - the object the user is writing or describing; - the minimum semantic facts required before generation is useful; - the modes that materially change how the input is interpreted; - the records, templates, or prior work a search mode should expose; - the two meaningfully different proposal strategies; - which completions may be generated freely and which must come from a trusted library; - what must remain editable and what always requires human confirmation. Do not ask about choices that can be inferred safely. Ask only when one of these values would materially alter the product. ## Preserve the core interaction model 1. Start as an almost empty white page with one instructional placeholder inside the writing surface. 2. Let the same surface accept a new description, an existing draft, pasted text, dictation, or an uploaded source when the product supports them. 3. Replace length thresholds with a transparent semantic completeness check. Ask one specific question for the first important missing fact, directly below the user's text. 4. Reveal the primary action only when the input is semantically sufficient or the current mode supports acting on partial text. 5. Open mode selection when the user types `/`. Make it compact, inline, filterable, and fully keyboard operable. 6. Render the chosen mode as bold inline text immediately before the input. It may be separate state internally, but Backspace at the start of the text must remove it as though it were adjacent text. 7. In search or record-selection modes, filter while the user types. Arrow keys move a visibly selected row; Enter adopts that row. 8. Offer inline autocomplete only when it has a safe next unit to suggest. Tab accepts; ordinary typing never gets intercepted. 9. After generation, present two clearly distinct, editable proposals with a binary choice. Do not create a gallery of near-duplicates. 10. Keep upload, dictation, and the contextual primary action in a restrained bottom bar so the page remains visually open. If the requested product does not need one of these capabilities, omit it rather than adding a decorative or inert control. ## Work in the existing codebase - Inspect the current framework, routing, design tokens, reusable components, and state conventions before implementing. - Preserve the existing architecture and package manager unless the user explicitly requests a replacement. - Separate domain rules from visual components. Completeness, mode interpretation, proposal composition, and trusted autocomplete should be testable without rendering the page. - Use one primary route and one coherent state model. Do not turn the experience into a dashboard or multi-step wizard unless the domain requires it. - Use trusted source IDs, provenance, or human-approval flags wherever the new domain requires traceability. Do not fabricate them to make a demo look complete. - Keep partial functionality honest. An upload control that does not extract content must say so; an unverified proposal must look unverified. ## Route to detailed guidance - Read [references/visual-language.md](references/visual-language.md) before creating or substantially restyling the page. - Read [references/interaction-contract.md](references/interaction-contract.md) when implementing modes, completeness questions, keyboard behavior, search, autocomplete, or proposal selection. - Read [references/implementation-and-acceptance.md](references/implementation-and-acceptance.md) when writing code, defining state, or validating the finished interaction. ## Completion standard The result should feel like writing on a clean sheet, not filling a form. A new user should be able to begin by typing without first understanding the product. Every revealed element must answer the current state: what can I type, what is missing, what can I choose, or what happens next. Validate compilation and relevant tests. For interaction changes, verify the keyboard-only path from empty page through mode selection, optional record selection, generation, proposal choice, editing, and reset. Report any capability that remains simulated or incomplete. --- name: minimal-writing-product-design description: Design or implement document-first web products that use a blank writing canvas, content-based follow-up questions, slash modes, keyboard-driven search, inline autocomplete, and a focused two-proposal decision. Use when a user wants the interaction logic of a minimalist AI writing workspace rather than a form, dashboard, wizard, or chat interface. --- # Minimal Writing Product Design Build the product around one continuous act of writing. Controls should appear only when the user's current state makes them useful. Preserve the user's domain, terminology, existing stack, and requested capabilities; reuse this interaction model without copying legal content or assuming a particular business process. ## Establish the product contract Before editing code, derive these domain-specific values from the request and repository: - the object the user is writing or describing; - the minimum semantic facts required before generation is useful; - the modes that materially change how the input is interpreted; - the records, templates, or prior work a search mode should expose; - the two meaningfully different proposal strategies; - which completions may be generated freely and which must come from a trusted library; - what must remain editable and what always requires human confirmation. Do not ask about choices that can be inferred safely. Ask only when one of these values would materially alter the product. ## Preserve the core interaction model 1. Start as an almost empty white page with one instructional placeholder inside the writing surface. 2. Let the same surface accept a new description, an existing draft, pasted text, dictation, or an uploaded source when the product supports them. 3. Replace length thresholds with a transparent semantic completeness check. Ask one specific question for the first important missing fact, directly below the user's text. 4. Reveal the primary action only when the input is semantically sufficient or the current mode supports acting on partial text. 5. Open mode selection when the user types `/`. Make it compact, inline, filterable, and fully keyboard operable. 6. Render the chosen mode as bold inline text immediately before the input. It may be separate state internally, but Backspace at the start of the text must remove it as though it were adjacent text. 7. In search or record-selection modes, filter while the user types. Arrow keys move a visibly selected row; Enter adopts that row. 8. Offer inline autocomplete only when it has a safe next unit to suggest. Tab accepts; ordinary typing never gets intercepted. 9. After generation, present two clearly distinct, editable proposals with a binary choice. Do not create a gallery of near-duplicates. 10. Keep upload, dictation, and the contextual primary action in a restrained bottom bar so the page remains visually open. If the requested product does not need one of these capabilities, omit it rather than adding a decorative or inert control. ## Work in the existing codebase - Inspect the current framework, routing, design tokens, reusable components, and state conventions before implementing. - Preserve the existing architecture and package manager unless the user explicitly requests a replacement. - Separate domain rules from visual components. Completeness, mode interpretation, proposal composition, and trusted autocomplete should be testable without rendering the page. - Use one primary route and one coherent state model. Do not turn the experience into a dashboard or multi-step wizard unless the domain requires it. - Use trusted source IDs, provenance, or human-approval flags wherever the new domain requires traceability. Do not fabricate them to make a demo look complete. - Keep partial functionality honest. An upload control that does not extract content must say so; an unverified proposal must look unverified. ## Route to detailed guidance - Read [references/visual-language.md](references/visual-language.md) before creating or substantially restyling the page. - Read [references/interaction-contract.md](references/interaction-contract.md) when implementing modes, completeness questions, keyboard behavior, search, autocomplete, or proposal selection. - Read [references/implementation-and-acceptance.md](references/implementation-and-acceptance.md) when writing code, defining state, or validating the finished interaction. ## Completion standard The result should feel like writing on a clean sheet, not filling a form. A new user should be able to begin by typing without first understanding the product. Every revealed element must answer the current state: what can I type, what is missing, what can I choose, or what happens next. Validate compilation and relevant tests. For interaction changes, verify the keyboard-only path from empty page through mode selection, optional record selection, generation, proposal choice, editing, and reset. Report any capability that remains simulated or incomplete. --- name: minimal-writing-product-design description: Design or implement document-first web products that use a blank writing canvas, content-based follow-up questions, slash modes, keyboard-driven search, inline autocomplete, and a focused two-proposal decision. Use when a user wants the interaction logic of a minimalist AI writing workspace rather than a form, dashboard, wizard, or chat interface. --- # Minimal Writing Product Design Build the product around one continuous act of writing. Controls should appear only when the user's current state makes them useful. Preserve the user's domain, terminology, existing stack, and requested capabilities; reuse this interaction model without copying legal content or assuming a particular business process. ## Establish the product contract Before editing code, derive these domain-specific values from the request and repository: - the object the user is writing or describing; - the minimum semantic facts required before generation is useful; - the modes that materially change how the input is interpreted; - the records, templates, or prior work a search mode should expose; - the two meaningfully different proposal strategies; - which completions may be generated freely and which must come from a trusted library; - what must remain editable and what always requires human confirmation. Do not ask about choices that can be inferred safely. Ask only when one of these values would materially alter the product. ## Preserve the core interaction model 1. Start as an almost empty white page with one instructional placeholder inside the writing surface. 2. Let the same surface accept a new description, an existing draft, pasted text, dictation, or an uploaded source when the product supports them. 3. Replace length thresholds with a transparent semantic completeness check. Ask one specific question for the first important missing fact, directly below the user's text. 4. Reveal the primary action only when the input is semantically sufficient or the current mode supports acting on partial text. 5. Open mode selection when the user types `/`. Make it compact, inline, filterable, and fully keyboard operable. 6. Render the chosen mode as bold inline text immediately before the input. It may be separate state internally, but Backspace at the start of the text must remove it as though it were adjacent text. 7. In search or record-selection modes, filter while the user types. Arrow keys move a visibly selected row; Enter adopts that row. 8. Offer inline autocomplete only when it has a safe next unit to suggest. Tab accepts; ordinary typing never gets intercepted. 9. After generation, present two clearly distinct, editable proposals with a binary choice. Do not create a gallery of near-duplicates. 10. Keep upload, dictation, and the contextual primary action in a restrained bottom bar so the page remains visually open. If the requested product does not need one of these capabilities, omit it rather than adding a decorative or inert control. ## Work in the existing codebase - Inspect the current framework, routing, design tokens, reusable components, and state conventions before implementing. - Preserve the existing architecture and package manager unless the user explicitly requests a replacement. - Separate domain rules from visual components. Completeness, mode interpretation, proposal composition, and trusted autocomplete should be testable without rendering the page. - Use one primary route and one coherent state model. Do not turn the experience into a dashboard or multi-step wizard unless the domain requires it. - Use trusted source IDs, provenance, or human-approval flags wherever the new domain requires traceability. Do not fabricate them to make a demo look complete. - Keep partial functionality honest. An upload control that does not extract content must say so; an unverified proposal must look unverified. ## Route to detailed guidance - Read [references/visual-language.md](references/visual-language.md) before creating or substantially restyling the page. - Read [references/interaction-contract.md](references/interaction-contract.md) when implementing modes, completeness questions, keyboard behavior, search, autocomplete, or proposal selection. - Read [references/implementation-and-acceptance.md](references/implementation-and-acceptance.md) when writing code, defining state, or validating the finished interaction. ## Completion standard The result should feel like writing on a clean sheet, not filling a form. A new user should be able to begin by typing without first understanding the product. Every revealed element must answer the current state: what can I type, what is missing, what can I choose, or what happens next. Validate compilation and relevant tests. For interaction changes, verify the keyboard-only path from empty page through mode selection, optional record selection, generation, proposal choice, editing, and reset. Report any capability that remains simulated or incomplete. # Visual language

Use this reference when designing or substantially restyling the writing workspace.

## Design intent

The interface should resemble a clean sheet of paper with intelligent behavior, not a form placed on a white background. Whitespace is functional: it gives the current sentence, follow-up question, or choice visual priority.

Avoid:

- cards around the main editor;
- persistent explanatory paragraphs;
- a dashboard shell inside the writing route;
- oversized marketing headlines;
- labeled input boxes for facts the user can express naturally;
- gradients, ornamental illustrations, or multiple accent colors;
- toolbars that appear before they are relevant;
- low-contrast selection states that are technically present but hard to see.

## Layout

Use these values as starting points, adapting them to the existing design system:

| Element | Recommended geometry |
|---|---|
| Page | full viewport, white background |
| Writing column | `max-width: 56rem`, centered |
| Comparison column | up to `72rem`, centered |
| Header | 4rem tall, visually quiet |
| Initial top offset | 7–10 viewport height units |
| Writing area | fills remaining height; never shrink it to the text height |
| Bottom action bar | fixed, minimum 5rem, full width |
| Bottom content padding | action-bar height plus safe-area inset |
| Slash/search menu | 20–24rem wide, aligned to the insertion area |

The textarea may autosize, but its containing writing surface must remain tall and clickable. Clicking unused white space should focus the input.

## Typography

Use typography to separate writing from interface mechanics:

- primary writing: readable serif or the product's editorial font, 1rem–1.25rem, line-height 1.7–1.85;
- inline mode: UI sans-serif, 0.875rem, bold;
- follow-up question: UI sans-serif, 0.8125–0.875rem, regular;
- menu title: UI sans-serif, 0.75–0.8125rem, semibold;
- secondary menu data: 0.625–0.75rem;
- provenance or IDs: monospace, 0.5625–0.6875rem.

Do not make the editor text look like a hero headline. On small screens, keep it near 1rem to preserve usable line length.

## Color tokens

Prefer neutral colors. If the host product already has accessible tokens, map these roles rather than introducing a parallel palette.

| Role | Example |
|---|---|
| Canvas | `#FFFFFF` |
| Primary text | slate 800–950 |
| Body text | slate 700–800 |
| Muted text | slate 400–500 |
| Placeholder | slate 300 |
| Hairline border | slate 100–200 |
| Selected row | slate 200 |
| Hovered row | slate 100 |
| Primary action | slate 950 with white text |
| Destructive/error | one restrained semantic red |

The selected keyboard row needs a visibly different filled background, normally at least slate 200. Do not rely on a border or a shade that is indistinguishable from white.

## Primary surface

The initial empty state contains only:

- the instructional placeholder;
- subtle navigation or product identity if the surrounding app requires it;
- the bottom input tools.

Once the user types, the placeholder disappears. Do not replace it with a heading. Render the next semantic question immediately below the user's current text, aligned with the text rather than in an alert box.

The active mode appears on the same visual line as the input. It is bold text, not a pill, badge, button, or outlined chip. If the mode plus selected record becomes long, truncate the label and preserve most width for writing.

## Menus

Slash and search menus are small transient overlays, not full selectors:

- white surface;
- 1px neutral border;
- 0.5–0.75rem corner radius;
- restrained shadow;
- compact 1.5–2.25rem rows;
- selected row filled with a clearly visible neutral gray;
- no checkboxes or radio circles unless selection persists after the menu closes.

For record results, show only the two identifiers needed to distinguish choices, usually title plus short ID or status. Put deeper information into the adopted context, not the result list.

## Bottom action bar

Anchor peripheral tools to the bottom edge. Use a white or 95% opaque white background with a single top hairline. Keep upload and dictation icon-only when familiar, with accessible labels and tooltips where appropriate.

The primary action appears at the opposite edge only when available. Use a compact rounded button, not a full-width banner on desktop. On mobile, allow a larger touch target while preserving the white-canvas feeling.

## Proposal comparison

After generation, shift from composing to deciding:

- one quiet instruction such as “Choose a proposal”;
- two equal-width proposals on desktop, stacked on narrow screens;
- a subtle divider rather than two heavy cards;
- a radio-like selection marker and a short strategy name;
- fully editable proposal text;
- unobtrusive provenance below each proposal;
- one adoption action visible only after selection.

The strategy labels must express a real tradeoff in the new product, such as concise/detailed, conservative/ambitious, or literal/adaptive. Do not label arbitrary variants A and B.

## Responsive and motion behavior

- Keep the editor, menus, and bottom bar usable at 320px width.
- Respect `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` for fixed mobile controls.
- Stack proposals below the layout breakpoint and remove the vertical divider.
- Ensure zoom to 200% does not hide the primary action or active menu row.
- Use transitions only for color, opacity, or small positional changes under 200ms.
- Respect reduced-motion preferences.

# Interaction contract

Use this reference when implementing input modes, completeness questions, keyboard behavior, searchable records, autocomplete, or proposal selection.

## State model

Model the experience explicitly. Names may vary, but the following states should remain distinguishable:

| State | User-visible behavior |
|---|---|
| Empty | instructional placeholder, peripheral tools only |
| Composing | user text, no unnecessary chrome |
| Incomplete | one inline question for the highest-priority missing fact |
| Ready | primary action becomes available |
| Slash menu | filtered mode commands with active row |
| Record search | filtered records with active row |
| Autocomplete | one safe ghost continuation with Tab hint |
| Generating | action shows progress without replacing user text |
| Comparing | two editable proposals and no composing footer |
| Adopted | selected proposal returns to an editable writing state |
| Error | local, actionable explanation; original input preserved |

Keep orthogonal state separate: input text, active mode, selected record, attachment, completeness, command query/index, record query/index, autocomplete, proposal texts, and selected proposal.

## Semantic completeness

Never use character count as the main readiness rule. Define 3–6 domain-specific semantic dimensions. Typical dimensions are:

- object or subject;
- observed event, desired operation, or concrete task;
- location, channel, source, or scope;
- affected audience or target;
- desired outcome or constraint;
- known exception or boundary when needed for safety.

The checker should return structured data, not just a boolean:

```ts
type Completeness = {
  complete: boolean;
  missing: string[];
  nextQuestion: string | null;
};
```

Ask only the first high-priority missing question. Questions must name the missing concept and preferably give two or three short examples. Do not ask generic prompts such as “Please provide more context.”

Use deterministic logic when possible. If an AI classifier is required, validate its output and preserve a deterministic fallback. Treat pasted existing output according to its mode; correction may be possible without all facts required for generation from scratch.

## Slash modes

Typing `/` at a valid command boundary opens the mode menu. Match only the current slash token, normally from `/` to the next whitespace. Filtering is case-insensitive and should search command plus human-readable title.

Recommended commands should describe interpretation, not pages. Examples:

- `/describe` — create from a new description;
- `/revise` — improve an existing draft;
- `/records` — select prior work or a trusted source.

Use the vocabulary and language of the product. Limit the initial list to modes that materially change behavior.

Keyboard contract:

| Key | Slash menu behavior |
|---|---|
| ArrowDown | select next visible command; wrap at end |
| ArrowUp | select previous visible command; wrap at start |
| Enter | adopt selected command; do not insert newline |
| Escape | close menu while preserving useful text |
| Pointer hover | synchronize the keyboard index |
| Pointer click | adopt clicked command |

Reset the active index to zero whenever the filtered query changes. If there are no results, show a compact empty message and let ordinary typing continue.

After adoption, remove the slash token, render the mode as bold inline text, and return focus to the editor. Internally storing the mode separately is acceptable and usually more robust than encoding it into the user's text.

Deletion contract:

- Backspace removes ordinary text normally.
- If the text cursor is at offset zero with no selection and a mode is active, Backspace removes the mode.
- Removing a mode also clears mode-specific selections and stale suggestions, but must not delete the user's remaining text.

## Searchable record mode

When a mode exposes records, templates, files, or prior work:

1. Start with a short useful subset or recent records.
2. Filter immediately as the user types a name or identifier.
3. Normalize case and product-appropriate diacritics consistently.
4. Keep the list small, usually five to eight results.
5. Show the minimum information needed to distinguish records.
6. Preserve the selected row while the query is unchanged.
7. Reset the selected index when the query or result set changes.

Keyboard contract mirrors the slash menu:

| Key | Record menu behavior |
|---|---|
| ArrowDown | select next result; wrap at end |
| ArrowUp | select previous result; wrap at start |
| Enter | adopt the highlighted result |
| Escape | leave record mode or close results, according to product intent |
| Pointer hover | synchronize selected index |

The highlighted record, not always the first result, must be adopted by Enter. Give the selected row a clearly visible background and expose selection semantics with `role="option"`, `aria-selected`, or an equivalent accessible pattern.

After adoption, show the selected record inline with the mode and populate or attach its context. Do not hide which source was chosen.

## Autocomplete

Autocomplete is a next-unit suggestion, not an unsolicited rewrite.

- Trigger after a short idle delay, usually 600–900ms.
- Suggest only in modes where continuation is meaningful.
- Prefer a trusted library, schema, or constrained operation when the domain demands provenance.
- Render the suggestion as low-emphasis ghost text directly below or after the current input.
- Tab accepts the suggestion; typing, Enter, arrow keys, and screen-reader navigation retain their ordinary meaning unless a higher-priority menu is open.
- Hide the suggestion when generation starts, the mode changes, or the text no longer matches its source context.

## Event priority

Handle keyboard events in this order so features do not conflict:

1. active slash-menu navigation and adoption;
2. active record-menu navigation and adoption;
3. mode deletion at text offset zero;
4. Escape behavior;
5. autocomplete acceptance with Tab;
6. ordinary editor behavior.

Ignore shortcut handling while an IME composition is active. Never capture arrow keys when no menu is open.

## Generation and proposal choice

The primary action becomes visible when:

- semantic completeness is satisfied; or
- the active correction/revision mode supports the current pasted draft; or
- a selected trusted record provides the required context; or
- an uploaded source has actually been processed sufficiently for the operation.

Do not treat the presence of a file name as extracted content.

Generation must preserve the original input until it succeeds. Disable duplicate submissions and show progress within the action. On failure, return to the same editable state with an actionable error.

Generate two proposals that differ along a named strategy dimension. Each proposal remains editable before adoption. Selection alone does not imply final approval; use a separate adoption or confirmation action. Preserve provenance, warnings, or manual-review status after editing.

## Reset and persistence

Reset clears text, mode, record, attachment, suggestions, proposal selection, and active indices. Confirm only when reset would discard substantial unsaved work and the surrounding product normally protects drafts.

If drafts persist, make persistence explicit and local to the product's existing data model. Do not add authentication, databases, or cloud storage merely to support this interaction pattern.

# Implementation and acceptance

Use this reference when writing code, structuring state, or validating the completed workspace.

## Recommended separation

Keep the primary route thin enough to understand. Extract domain logic into pure functions or services:

```text
route/page component
├─ writing surface and menus
├─ state transitions
├─ completeness checker (pure)
├─ mode/record search (pure)
├─ autocomplete source (pure or service)
├─ proposal builder/client
└─ provenance and approval model
```

Avoid one generic “AI response” state. Proposal content, source IDs, warnings, and selection are separate values with separate lifecycle rules.

## Framework-neutral state shape

Adapt this model rather than copying it verbatim:

```ts
type WorkspaceState<Mode, Record, Proposal> = {
  text: string;
  mode: Mode | null;
  selectedRecord: Record | null;
  attachment: { name: string; status: "selected" | "processing" | "ready" | "failed" } | null;
  completeness: {
    complete: boolean;
    missing: string[];
    nextQuestion: string | null;
  };
  commandMenu: { open: boolean; query: string; index: number };
  recordMenu: { open: boolean; query: string; index: number };
  autocomplete: { text: string; sourceId?: string } | null;
  generation: "idle" | "running" | "failed";
  proposals: [Proposal, Proposal] | null;
  selectedProposal: 0 | 1 | null;
};
```

Use a reducer or explicit transition functions when several state values must change together. In small components, grouped setters are acceptable if every transition clears stale mode-specific state.

## Editor implementation

A controlled textarea is sufficient for plain text. To autosize:

1. set its height to zero or `auto` after value changes;
2. read `scrollHeight`;
3. set the measured height with a sensible one-line minimum.

Keep a tall parent writing surface and focus the textarea when its empty area is clicked. Do not make the textarea itself fill the entire viewport if doing so breaks autosizing or caret behavior.

For the inline mode, prefer a flex row with a non-editable bold prefix and a textarea. This provides stable state and predictable deletion. Implement Backspace-at-zero semantics explicitly. Use a richer editor only when the product genuinely requires mixed formatting inside the document.

## Menu implementation

Derive menu visibility and query from the text when practical; store only the active index. For each menu:

- give the container `role="listbox"` or an equivalent menu role;
- give rows stable keys and selection semantics;
- keep DOM order equal to keyboard order;
- reset index when the query changes;
- clamp or wrap the index when results change;
- make hover update the same index used by Enter;
- return focus to the editor after adoption;
- scroll the active row into view if the result list can overflow.

Do not use placeholder color as the only indication of selection.

## Completeness implementation

Represent each required fact as a named predicate. Keep the priority order explicit:

```ts
const checks = {
  subject: hasSubject(input),
  action: hasAction(input),
  scope: hasScope(input),
  outcome: hasDesiredOutcome(input),
};

const nextQuestion = !checks.subject
  ? questions.subject
  : !checks.action
    ? questions.action
    : !checks.scope
      ? questions.scope
      : !checks.outcome
        ? questions.outcome
        : null;
```

Regexes are acceptable for a bounded prototype, but document recognized terms and limitations. For production, prefer structured extraction with a validated schema and deterministic fallbacks. Unit-test semantic cases, not word count.

## Proposal implementation

The proposal builder should receive structured context and an explicit strategy. Return data rather than only a string:

```ts
type Proposal = {
  strategy: string;
  text: string;
  sourceIds: string[];
  warnings: string[];
  humanApprovalRequired: boolean;
};
```

If no safe source or template applies, return an unsupported result and say so in the UI. Never fabricate source IDs, citations, records, or approval.

## Accessibility requirements

- The writing surface has an accessible name even when its placeholder is gone.
- Icon-only buttons have explicit labels.
- Keyboard menus expose selection to assistive technology.
- Focus remains visible and is not obscured by the fixed bottom bar.
- Text and selected-row contrast meet WCAG AA.
- Status changes such as generation failure use an appropriate live region without announcing every keystroke.
- Touch targets are at least 40–44px where icons are the only control.
- The experience works without dictation, drag-and-drop, hover, or a pointer.

## Acceptance matrix

Test at least these paths:

### Empty and composition

- Empty page shows one instructional placeholder and no premature primary action.
- Typing removes the placeholder without moving the writing surface unexpectedly.
- Clicking unused white space focuses the editor.
- A short but complete input becomes ready.
- A long but semantically incomplete input shows the correct single question.
- The question appears directly below the user's text.

### Slash modes

- `/` opens the full command list.
- Additional letters filter commands.
- ArrowDown and ArrowUp move a clearly visible selection and wrap correctly.
- Enter adopts the highlighted command, not always the first command.
- Hover and keyboard use the same active index.
- The chosen mode appears inline and focus returns to the editor.
- Backspace at text offset zero removes the mode without deleting user text.

### Record selection

- The record mode shows a small initial result set.
- Typing a title or ID filters the set.
- Arrow keys move the highlighted record and wrap correctly.
- Enter adopts the highlighted record.
- Hover synchronizes the highlighted index.
- Changing the query resets selection safely.
- An empty result displays a compact message without trapping the user.

### Autocomplete

- Suggestion appears only after its debounce and only in eligible modes.
- Tab accepts it.
- Tab does not accept stale text after mode or context changes.
- Arrow keys remain ordinary caret keys when no menu is open.

### Generation and proposals

- Primary action appears only under documented readiness conditions.
- Duplicate generation is prevented while running.
- Failure preserves the original text and offers a useful recovery.
- Exactly two meaningfully distinct proposals appear.
- Both proposals are independently editable.
- Adoption requires an explicit selection and confirmation.
- Required provenance and human-review state remain visible.

### Responsive and regression

- The fixed bottom bar never covers the caret, question, or final line.
- Menus fit a 320px viewport and remain keyboard accessible at 200% zoom.
- Proposal comparison stacks cleanly on mobile.
- Reset clears every state branch and returns to the initial placeholder.
- Existing routes, application shell, and unrelated product behavior remain unchanged.

## Verification depth

Run the repository's formatter, type checker, build, and relevant unit tests. Add tests for pure completeness and transition logic. Use browser automation only when requested or when the local workflow explicitly requires it; otherwise verify the route responds and report that visual interaction still needs human inspection.

When handing off, state:

- which domain completeness dimensions were chosen;
- which modes and searchable records were implemented;
- the strategy difference between the two proposals;
- which inputs are genuinely processed versus merely displayed;
- what remains simulated, unverified, or dependent on human approval.

class HumanReviewRepository:
    def __init__(self, database_path: str | Path) -> None:
        self.database_path = Path(database_path).resolve()
        self.database_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with self._connection() as connection:
            connection.execute("""CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS human_reviews (
                case_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, decision TEXT NOT NULL, decided_at TEXT NOT NULL)""")

    @contextmanager
    def _connection(self):
        connection = sqlite3.connect(self.database_path)
        connection.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        try:
            with connection:
                yield connection
        finally:
            connection.close()

    def save(self, case_id: str, decision: str) -> None:
        if decision not in DECISIONS:
            raise ValueError("Unzulässige menschliche Entscheidung.")
        with self._connection() as connection:
            connection.execute("""INSERT INTO human_reviews(case_id, decision, decided_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?)
                ON CONFLICT(case_id) DO UPDATE SET decision=excluded.decision,
                decided_at=excluded.decided_at""",
                (case_id, decision, datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()))

    def get(self, case_id: str) -> dict | None:
        with self._connection() as connection:
            row = connection.execute(
                "SELECT decision, decided_at FROM human_reviews WHERE case_id = ?", (case_id,)
            ).fetchone()
        return dict(row) if row else None


class TenorDraftRepository:
    def __init__(self, database_path: str | Path) -> None:
        self.database_path = Path(database_path).resolve()
        self.database_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with self._connection() as connection:
            connection.execute("""CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tenor_drafts (
                draft_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
                mode TEXT NOT NULL,
                model TEXT NOT NULL,
                input_json TEXT NOT NULL,
                draft_json TEXT NOT NULL,
                decision TEXT,
                decided_at TEXT)""")

    @contextmanager
    def _connection(self):
        connection = sqlite3.connect(self.database_path)
        connection.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        try:
            with connection:
                yield connection
        finally:
            connection.close()

    def save(
        self, model_input: dict, draft: TenorDraft, *, mode: str, model: str
    ) -> dict:
        record = {
            "draft_id": uuid.uuid4().hex,
            "created_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
            "mode": mode,
            "model": model,
            "input": model_input,
            "draft": draft.to_dict(),
            "decision": None,
            "decided_at": None,
        }
        with self._connection() as connection:
            connection.execute(
                """INSERT INTO tenor_drafts(
                    draft_id, created_at, mode, model, input_json, draft_json
                ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
                (
                    record["draft_id"], record["created_at"], mode, model,
                    json.dumps(model_input, ensure_ascii=False),
                    json.dumps(record["draft"], ensure_ascii=False),
                ),
            )
        return record

    def latest(self) -> dict | None:
        with self._connection() as connection:
            row = connection.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM tenor_drafts ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1"
            ).fetchone()
        return self._decode(row) if row else None

    def get(self, draft_id: str) -> dict:
        if not re.fullmatch(r"[a-f0-9]{32}", draft_id):
            raise ValueError("Tenor-Entwurf nicht gefunden.")
        with self._connection() as connection:
            row = connection.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM tenor_drafts WHERE draft_id = ?", (draft_id,)
            ).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            raise ValueError("Tenor-Entwurf nicht gefunden.")
        return self._decode(row)

    def decide(self, draft_id: str, decision: str) -> dict:
        if decision not in DECISIONS:
            raise ValueError("Unzulässige menschliche Entscheidung.")
        decided_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
        with self._connection() as connection:
            cursor = connection.execute(
                """UPDATE tenor_drafts SET decision = ?, decided_at = ?
                WHERE draft_id = ?""",
                (decision, decided_at, draft_id),
            )
            if cursor.rowcount != 1:
                raise ValueError("Tenor-Entwurf nicht gefunden.")
        return self.get(draft_id)

    @staticmethod
    def _decode(row: sqlite3.Row) -> dict:
        return {
            "draft_id": row["draft_id"],
            "created_at": row["created_at"],
            "mode": row["mode"],
            "model": row["model"],
            "input": json.loads(row["input_json"]),
            "draft": json.loads(row["draft_json"]),
            "decision": row["decision"],
            "decided_at": row["decided_at"],
        }
